podcast.title: Arkansas Rockabilly in Canada
podcast.body: Ronnie Hawkins, an Arkansas rockabilly musician, relocated to Canada in the late 1950s and significantly impacted rock and roll music. "Ronnie Hawkins, the Arkansas rockabilly, who moved to Canada in the late 1950s and changed so much about rock and roll."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam of Those Lost in 2022

podcast.title: Dale Hawkins' Cousin and Musical Career
podcast.body: Ronnie Hawkins, a cousin of Dale Hawkins, pursued his own musical career which would later intersect with several other notable artists in the music industry. "Another family member, Ronnie Hawkins, would later have his own musical career, which would intersect with several of the artists we're going to be looking at later in this series."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Death from Natural Causes
podcast.body: Ronnie Hawkins died on May 28th at the age of 87, not from pancreatic cancer, but because his body simply gave out after years of a hard rock and roll lifestyle. "And when he died on May 28th at the age of 87, it wasn't from pancreatic cancer. After years of hard rock and roll in his body, he just gave out."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam of Those Lost in 2022

podcast.title: Formation of The Hawks
podcast.body: Ronnie Hawkins assembled a band called The Hawks, which was later recruited by Bob Dylan and eventually became The Band. "He put together a band called The Hawks, who were later poached by Bob Dylan and later became The Band, one of the most influential bands of the 60s and 70s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam of Those Lost in 2022

podcast.title: Pancreatic Cancer Remission
podcast.body: Diagnosed with pancreatic cancer in 2002, Ronnie Hawkins credited a 15-year-old faith healer from Vancouver for his pancreatic cancer going into remission for many years. "He was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer in 2002. But thanks to a 15 year old faith healer from Vancouver, or so Ronnie says, that pancreatic cancer went into remission for years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Recording at The Bath House
podcast.body: Ronnie Hawkins recorded at The Bath House, The Tragically Hip's residential studio. "Blue rodeo, Ronnie Hawkins, Sam Roberts, Big Rec, and dozens and dozens of others have worked there."

xref.title: Early Musical Influences
xref.body: While initially struggling to find music he liked despite a musical household, by age 15, Declan McManus became a fan of The Grateful Dead and The Band, a Canadian group known for backing Ronnie Hawkins and Bob Dylan. These influences shaped his early musical interests before he gravitated towards punk and new wave. "By the time he was 15, though, he had become something of a fan of the grateful dead. He also was a big fan of the band, that Canadian group that backed up both Ronnie Hawkins and Bob Dylan."
